title: Interpret checks without overstating integrity
goal: Separate package verification, database audit and a learner-copy checksum.
challenge: Verify coreutils content metadata and audit package state, then demonstrate a mismatch on a learner-owned copy. Explain what each result establishes and why none alone authenticates the system. Do not modify installed coreutils.

steps.command: w=/home/learner/ll-discovery-6; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
steps.explanation: Create a fresh private workspace; stop on collision or insufficient space.
steps.expected: Exact learner path, no existing entry, at least64MiB free.

steps.command: guard() { local links; test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-discovery-6 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-discovery-6 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && links=$(sudo find . -type l -print -quit) && test -z "$links"; }; guard
steps.expected: No path substitution; guest root can override guest safeguards.

steps.command: unrelated() { dpkg-query -W -f='${binary:Package}\t${Version}\t${db:Status-Status}\n' | awk '$1!="ll-discovery-data" && $1!="ll-discovery-report"'; }; unrelated > before.tsv; sudo sha256sum /etc/sudoers.d/learning-lab > sudo.before; id learner > learner.before; scope_ok() { guard && unrelated > after.tsv && cmp before.tsv after.tsv && sudo sha256sum -c sudo.before && id learner > learner.after && cmp learner.before learner.after; }; scope_ok
steps.explanation: Retain unrelated package and learner/sudo evidence before any transaction.
steps.expected: Protected unrelated state captured; stop on mismatch.

steps.command: guard && dpkg --verify coreutils > verification.txt; rc=$?; printf 'verify status=%s\n' "$rc"; cat verification.txt; dpkg --audit > audit.txt; printf 'audit status=%s\n' "$?"; cat audit.txt
steps.explanation: dpkg verification uses recorded MD5 content metadata where available; audit checks package state.
steps.expected: On a fresh guest both are quiet/status0. This is not authenticity or a complete permissions/security audit.

steps.command: guard && test ! -e note.txt && printf 'original\n' > note.txt && sha256sum note.txt > expected.sha256 && sha256sum -c expected.sha256
steps.explanation: This reference concerns only your own file, not an installed package.
steps.expected: An initial match against your retained reference.

steps.command: guard && printf 'changed\n' > note.txt && sha256sum -c expected.sha256; printf 'comparison status=%s\n' "$?"
steps.explanation: Intentionally alter only this learner-owned copy.
steps.expected: Mismatch/nonzero status; actual package-owned damage and reinstallation come in Lesson8.

hints: No output is scoped to metadata and checks actually performed.
A writable checksum reference does not authenticate content.
Changing note.txt is not a dpkg verification experiment.
review: Statuses, scoped interpretation and learner-file mismatch; coreutils unchanged.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 102.4 partial integrity/state inspection; checksum reinforcement. Self-reviewed, unscored; not complete objectives.
